Hi Samantha / team,

Thanks again for the call this morning — great to hear how the upcoming feature rollout will change your consumption profile. Per our ask, I attached a first-pass SOW and a short pricing spreadsheet with three alternate approaches for the renewal term. High level: we designed one option to protect you with a usage floor and quarterly true-ups, and two alternatives that shift more cost to annual precommitments.

Quick summary (details in attachment):
- Option A — Staggered uplift + usage floor (recommended): 10% uplift on committed units in Q1, additional 10% in Q3; 85% usage floor with quarterly true-up and carry-forward credits.
- Option B — Annualize top-up: single top-up at renewal with blended discount (higher up-front discount; less flexible).
- Option C — Co-term + burst buffer: keep co-terming with a fixed burst buffer and overage pricing.

As discussed, please confirm procurement timing and whether we should include the SOC2 addendum and the data processing addendum in the SOW. Goal from our side is to get a signed SOW + PO by 10/01 to enable the capacity reservations for your Q4 rollout.

Attachments: HV_SOW_draft_v1.pdf, pricing-models-spreadsheet.xlsx

Next steps:

- Irene/Jordan: internal quick check on margin and SLA carveouts (Jordan, tagging you for approval on the staged uplift discount)

Thanks —

Thanks Samantha — good questions. I summarized the operational mechanics and included a worked example below so procurement can map to their PO process. Ben — see Jordan for quick approval on the discounting assumptions.

Operational mechanics (Option A — Staggered uplift + quarterly true-up):
- Commitment windows: Q1 (months 1–3) = base commit + 10% uplift; Q2 = base commit; Q3 = base commit + additional 10% uplift; Q4 = base commit.
- Usage floor: 85% of committed units per 12-month rolling period. If total annualized usage < floor, invoice is for floor amount but carry-forward credits (up to 25% of difference) are granted to the following quarter.
- Quarterly true-up: usage measured on the 10th business day after quarter close, invoice adjustment netted on next invoice. Overage rates are defined in the spreadsheet.

Worked example (annualized):
- Base commit: 1M tokens/month => 12M tokens annual
- Q1 uplift 10% => committed tokens Q1 = 1.1M/month; Q3 uplift similarly applied
- If actual usage = 9.6M tokens for year (80% utilization), floor triggers (85% = 10.2M), invoice charges 10.2M less carry-forward credits; carry-forward % up to 25% applied to next quarter's uplift balance.

Pricing: Ben, per Samantha request, we should add a per-unit effective price table to the spreadsheet. Jordan — can you confirm if we can hold the staged uplift discount at 7.5% on the uplifted units and keep list pricing for baseline units? If not, recommend callout.

Legal: will attach SOC2 addendum and DPA; procurement asked that those be included in the DocuSign bundle.
